title: Subdomain takeover: ellen.withspotify.com CNAMEs to a dangling Heroku custom-domain target
vulnerability_information:
**Summary**
`ellen.withspotify.com` is a `*.withspotify.com` hostname in Spotify's in-scope wildcard. It still carries a `CNAME` to Heroku's automated-certificate target for that exact custom domain, but the domain is no longer attached to any Heroku app — the DNS target returns NODATA. Because Heroku derives that target deterministically from the custom domain, any Heroku account that adds `ellen.withspotify.com` as a custom domain receives the *same* `CNAME` target, and traffic to the Spotify hostname is then served from attacker-controlled content.

**Steps to reproduce / verification** (2026-11-07T16:30Z, passive only — nothing registered, nothing changed):

```
$ dig +short ellen.withspotify.com CNAME
ellen.withspotify.com.herokudns.com.

$ dig ellen.withspotify.com.herokudns.com A
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR   <- zone exists, but no record for this name
;; ANSWER SECTION: (empty)

$ curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://ellen.withspotify.com/
000            <- connection fails: the CNAME target has no A/AAAA record
```

The record is served by Heroku's DNS (`herokudns.com` is delegated to `dns1/dns2.p05.nsone.net`), so the zone is live while the per-domain record has been removed. That is the signature of a custom domain that was deleted from a Heroku app while the customer-side `CNAME` was left in place.

**Why it is exploitable**
Heroku's custom-domain target is a function of the domain name, not of the app. An attacker who creates a Heroku app and adds `ellen.withspotify.com` as a custom domain obtains the identical `herokudns.com` target, after which `ellen.withspotify.com` resolves to the attacker's dyno. No DNS access to `withspotify.com` is required, and the Spotify-owned certificate path is not needed either — the attacker can serve plain HTTP, or complete Heroku's ACM issuance for a name they do not own, since the `CNAME` already points at Heroku.

**Impact**
Arbitrary content on a `spotify.com`-branded hostname under `*.withspotify.com`: credential phishing, malicious downloads, and any functionality that trusts a `*.withspotify.com` origin. If any Spotify-issued cookie is scoped to a parent domain that covers this host, that cookie content can also be read from the attacker-controlled page.

**Remediation**
Remove the dangling `ellen.withspotify.com` `CNAME`, or re-attach the custom domain to a Heroku app you control so the target resolves. An inventory pass over `*.withspotify.com` for other `herokudns.com`/`herokuapp.com` records is advisable.

I have not created any Heroku app, added the domain anywhere, or published any content; this report is based solely on public DNS and a single `GET`.
impact: Arbitrary attacker-controlled content on an in-scope Spotify-branded hostname (phishing, malicious downloads, origin trust abuse for *.withspotify.com).
